idiom_name: Map[String, Decoder[_]] + Kafka Headers, circe decoding
implementation_notes: circe's default ADT support decodes by trying the case-class decoders in order, or with a discriminator field added to the JSON via generic-extras withDiscriminator - both content-based. The property-based form reads the record header and selects a Decoder[_] from a hand-written Map keyed by token, then decodes once; sealed traits plus pattern matching keep the registry closed and Scala's exhaustiveness checking keeps it honest. Nothing in the ecosystem supplies this channel, so the classic structure is hand-written, with the header read from the Kafka client.
pitfalls: Decoder[_] is existential, so the cast to Decoder[Event] is unavoidable unless the registry stores Decoder[Event] via widen/emap - hide it behind one registry type instead of casting at every call site.
generic-extras withDiscriminator adds the token as a payload field; if both the header and that field can be set they will disagree, and the payload wins silently.
Shapeless-based derivation tries constructors in alphabetical order and is documented to mis-pick ambiguous case classes, so that ordering must never be the type-selection mechanism.
